title: Comparison of 1 Versus 2 Doses of Quadrivalent Influenza Vaccine in 3-8-Year-Old Children with Different Immunological States - Jiangsu Province, China, 2021.
ehr_evidence: In this open-label, self-paired clinical trial conducted in Donghai County, Jiangsu Province, China (ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT05313893), we enrolled healthy children aged 3–8 years.
summary: Open-label, self-paired clinical trial comparing immunogenicity and safety of one versus two doses of quadrivalent influenza vaccine in children aged 3–8 years, stratified by prior vaccination history.
key_findings: Group A (previously vaccinated) showed GMT fold increases of 4.84–8.51 after dose 1, with slight decreases after dose 2 for H1N1 (0.92-fold, 95% CI: 0.85, 0.99) and BV (0.86-fold, 95% CI: 0.80, 0.93).

Group B (vaccine-naive) showed GMT fold increases of 6.09–20.41 after dose 1, with further increases after dose 2 for H1N1 (1.48-fold, 95% CI: 1.04, 1.31), BY (2.15-fold, 95% CI: 1.74, 2.66), and BV (1.57-fold, 95% CI: 1.33, 1.84).
Baseline serostatus significantly impacted antibody titers, with seropositive individuals consistently exhibiting higher titers regardless of dosage.
Adverse reaction incidence was 38.8% in Group A and 22.5% in Group B over 28 days, with no serious adverse events reported.
population: children aged 3–8 years in Jiangsu Province, China
limitations: failure to investigate the durability of immune responses following vaccination
lack of randomized comparison between one and two doses for long-term durability
data_availability_statement: Supplementary data to this article can be found online.
